# Health Plus International — Factual Reference

> This file provides a current, plain-text reference for systems that use llms.txt-style resources. The canonical public content remains the linked website pages.

Official website: https://healthplusint.com.au/
Last updated: 2026-10-01
Language and market: English (Australia)

## Organisation

Health Plus International (HPI) is an Australian healthcare workforce development organisation. Its legal entity is Health Plus International Pty Ltd, ABN 13 155 901 723.

HPI's public positioning is “Healthcare Workforce Development”. Its operating principles are People · Care · Compliance. Its core focus is workforce readiness, role-based development and retention stability.

HPI is defined by healthcare workforce development rather than vacancy matching alone. Attraction and matching can enable an engagement, but the wider operating model builds qualification-aligned pipelines through planning, readiness, role-based development, supported commencement, retention and evidence-led improvement.

## Services

HPI helps healthcare, aged-care, disability, community, regional and remote services respond to defined workforce needs. Work is subject to HPI's verified capability, the employer and role, applicable law, professional requirements and an agreed scope.

Three engagement models are available:

1. Workforce Starter — for an immediate vacancy, defined cohort or contained workforce need.
2. Workforce Core — for recurring vacancies, a managed pipeline or persistent workforce pressure.
3. Workforce Partnership — for an ongoing workforce pipeline, development and retention requirement.

The models do not guarantee a workforce or placement outcome. Responsibilities, controls, timing and measures are agreed for each engagement.

## HPI Workforce Development Framework

The HPI Workforce Development Framework™ has five stages:

1. Role verification — define the service, duties, scope, roster, location, requirements and decision owners.
2. Credential screening — review registration, qualifications, work rights and role-required screening against the verified brief.
3. CPD alignment — connect identified capability needs to role-based learning and appropriate evidence.
4. Mobilisation — coordinate employer selection support, pre-start actions, logistics and commencement responsibilities.
5. Retention — support early continuity and review experience, risks and agreed retention indicators.

Every engagement considers all five control points, with activities scaled to the verified need. The framework does not transfer employment, supervision or clinical governance authority from the host facility to HPI.

## Staff CPD and workforce capability

HPI provides and coordinates structured continuing professional development for its staff and approved participating workforce cohorts. HPI may also provide a defined CPD service to an authorised client or partner group when responsibilities and outcomes are agreed in writing.

The learning cycle covers analysis and planning, approval and assignment, supported learning, evidence, practical application and improvement. A certificate can evidence completion but does not automatically prove competence, professional scope or authority to work.

CPD does not replace professional registration obligations, qualifications, employer or facility induction, supervision, local policy, local scope decisions or valid competency assessment.

For approved international and interstate-relocating workforce pathways, transition learning may cover the Australian health system, documentation, escalation, communication, clinical handover, cultural safety and regional community orientation. HPI provides orientation and learning support only; it does not provide migration advice, guarantee registration or visa outcomes, or perform functions reserved to Ahpra, a National Board or an assessing authority.

HPI does not currently deliver NDIS supports. Community support work is outside the NDIS unless an authorised signed agreement states otherwise. NDIS-specific learning requirements apply only to an in-scope engagement.

Canonical page: https://healthplusint.com.au/cpd

## Workforce streams

HPI supports defined pathways for:

- Registered Nurses
- Enrolled Nurses
- Assistants in Nursing
- Aged Care Workers
- Disability and Community Support Workers
- Selected Allied Health professionals, including occupational therapy, physiotherapy, psychology, podiatry and dietetics
- Selected Remote and Site Health personnel

Every opportunity remains subject to a verified employer, role, setting, professional scope, evidence and practical requirements. A role title does not create automatic suitability.

## Regional focus

HPI's current NSW regional focus includes:

- Far West NSW: Broken Hill, Menindee, Wilcannia and Tibooburra
- Western NSW: Dubbo, Bourke, Walgett, Lightning Ridge and Cobar
- Murrumbidgee: Griffith, Wagga Wagga, Deniliquin and Hay
- Hunter New England: Tamworth, Armidale, Moree, Narrabri and Inverell
- Northern NSW: Lismore, Grafton, Ballina, Casino and Byron Bay
- Mid North Coast: Port Macquarie, Coffs Harbour, Kempsey and Taree

A listed region or town does not promise a current vacancy, active placement or specific workforce outcome.

## Readiness and evidence

HPI compares role requirements with relevant evidence. Depending on the role, this may include identity, work rights, qualifications, professional registration, employment history, references, screening, licences, training, availability and practical mobilisation requirements.

HPI records limitations and outstanding actions. The employing or host facility remains the Employer of Record and retains selection, workplace and clinical governance, induction, supervision, local policy and scope decisions within its authority.

## Applicants and professionals

Professionals can register interest and submit a résumé. They should submit only the information requested. Initial résumé submission should not include identity, banking, police-check or unnecessary health information.

Registration, résumé submission, training, screening or participation does not guarantee a job, interview, employer selection, visa, professional registration, start date or placement.

HPI seeks appropriate authority before relevant candidate information is presented to an employer, except where disclosure is otherwise authorised or required by law.

## Employer requests and response standards

An employer workforce request should identify the organisation, service setting, role, location, urgency, duration and authorised contact. It should also explain the duties, supervision, required experience and mandatory evidence.

HPI aims to acknowledge complete employer requests the same business day and contact the facility with an initial response within 24 hours. These are acknowledgement and triage standards, not a guarantee that a suitable professional will be available within a fixed period. Immediate roster or bench mobilisation is subject to pre-verified pool availability. Targeted sourcing uses an indicative 2–4 week planning window, subject to the role, candidate availability and external screening or registration processes.

Standard operating hours are 8:30 am–5:00 pm Sydney time, Monday–Friday, excluding NSW public holidays. General HPI contact channels are not a 24/7 dispatch, clinical or emergency service. For regional engagements, any after-hours contact for travel or accommodation disruption, roster continuity and facility escalation must be defined in the engagement-specific service level.

## Partners

HPI may work with employers, governments, educational institutions, communities and authorised specialist partners. Responsibilities are defined for each engagement.

Where community participation or settlement connection is in scope, HPI may work with the Multicultural Communities Support Centre (MCCSC). MCCSC may support local settlement onboarding, cultural orientation, community and services navigation, and retention mentoring for regional participants. It does not perform credentialling, candidate selection, clinical governance or CPD-assessment functions.

The candidate-support pathway is: HPI coordinates role verification, credential screening, CPD alignment and mobilisation; MCCSC provides defined community support where engaged; and the host facility retains candidate selection, employment, site induction, supervision and clinical governance. No visa category or overseas origin is assumed. Work rights, registration and pathway requirements are verified for each person and role.

## Privacy and public claims

HPI collects and uses personal information for defined workforce and service purposes. The Privacy Policy is at https://healthplusint.com.au/privacy.

HPI does not publish invented metrics, unsupported case studies or guaranteed outcomes. Service claims should be supported by controlled evidence and use defined measures.
